# T6.2 (TASKS.md) -- DESIGN.md §3 degenerate-case table, row "Two nodes
# both believe they're heir (stale announcement across heir change)": a
# heir-change announcement reaches one follower but not the other (message
# genuinely lost, via deliver-msgs drop), so one node still believes the
# *old* heir assignment (itself) while the other correctly believes the
# *new* one (also itself). Both then race on the heir-biased fast timeout
# and split the vote -- "same as vanilla split candidacy" -- before a
# second, ordinary round resolves it cleanly. Round two's winner is pinned
# via set-randomized-election-timeout rather than left to the real PRNG, so
# the golden file is deterministic; DESIGN.md's "resolved by randomized
# jitter" is the real mechanism this stands in for.
#
# min-heir-tenure=1 lets the second heir change (2 -> 3, after node 3's
# score is bumped) take effect on the very next heartbeat instead of
# waiting out the default 10-interval hysteresis window -- irrelevant to
# what this test is about, so kept out of the way.

log-level error
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3) index=2 heir-election=true stability-score=50 min-heir-tenure=1
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3) index=2 heir-election=true mutable-stability-score=200 min-heir-tenure=1
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3) index=2 heir-election=true mutable-stability-score=50 min-heir-tenure=1
----
ok

campaign 1
----
ok

# First selection: 2 (200) beats 3 (50) -- heir=2, announced to both.

# 3's score jumps well past 2's by more than the hysteresis margin.
set-stability-score 3 score=255
----
ok

# This heartbeat round still re-selects using the *old* scores -- selectHeir
# runs synchronously inside tick-heartbeat, before 3's updated-score
# response for this very round has even been delivered. heir stays 2.
# Delivered to everyone: it changes nothing 2 doesn't already believe, so
# there's nothing to protect it from.
tick-heartbeat 1
----
ok

status 1
----
1: StateReplicate match=3 next=4
2: StateReplicate match=3 next=4 score=200
3: StateReplicate match=3 next=4 score=255
heir=2 churn=0

# The leader now knows 3's new score, and this round's selection sees 3 as
# a genuine challenger for the first time -- but changeHeir's hysteresis
# gate (raft.go selectHeir) requires r.heirTenure >= MinHeirTenure(1), and
# tenure only starts accumulating once a challenger has been seen at all
# (it isn't simply "rounds since heir was picked"): a bare "still winning,
# no challenger" round never touches it. So this round just registers the
# challenge (tenure 0 -> 1) without swapping yet. Delivered to everyone:
# heir is still 2, changing nothing 2 doesn't already believe.
tick-heartbeat 1
----
ok

stabilize
----
> 1 handling Ready
  Ready MustSync=false:
  Messages:
  1->2 MsgHeartbeat Term:1 Log:0/0 Commit:3
  1->3 MsgHeartbeat Term:1 Log:0/0 Commit:3
> 2 receiving messages
  1->2 MsgHeartbeat Term:1 Log:0/0 Commit:3
> 3 receiving messages
  1->3 MsgHeartbeat Term:1 Log:0/0 Commit:3
> 2 handling Ready
  Ready MustSync=false:
  Messages:
  2->1 MsgHeartbeatResp Term:1 Log:0/0
> 3 handling Ready
  Ready MustSync=false:
  Messages:
  3->1 MsgHeartbeatResp Term:1 Log:0/0
> 1 receiving messages
  2->1 MsgHeartbeatResp Term:1 Log:0/0
  3->1 MsgHeartbeatResp Term:1 Log:0/0

status 1
----
1: StateReplicate match=3 next=4
2: StateReplicate match=3 next=4 score=200
3: StateReplicate match=3 next=4 score=255
heir=2 churn=0

# *Now* tenure(1) >= MinHeirTenure(1) and the margin is still satisfied, so
# this heartbeat tick's selection genuinely flips the heir to 3. This is
# the round that must be kept from node 2 -- delivered to 1 and 3 only.
tick-heartbeat 1
----
ok

stabilize 1 3
----
> 1 handling Ready
  Ready MustSync=false:
  Messages:
  1->2 MsgHeartbeat Term:1 Log:0/0 Commit:3
  1->3 MsgHeartbeat Term:1 Log:0/0 Commit:3
> 3 receiving messages
  1->3 MsgHeartbeat Term:1 Log:0/0 Commit:3
> 3 handling Ready
  Ready MustSync=false:
  Messages:
  3->1 MsgHeartbeatResp Term:1 Log:0/0
> 1 receiving messages
  3->1 MsgHeartbeatResp Term:1 Log:0/0

# The heartbeat addressed to 2 for this round is still sitting undelivered
# in the queue -- drop it outright (message genuinely lost in transit, not
# merely delayed) so no later stabilize call can accidentally resurrect it
# and hand 2 the update after all.
deliver-msgs drop=(2)
----
dropped: 1->2 MsgHeartbeat Term:1 Log:0/0 Commit:3

status 1
----
1: StateReplicate match=3 next=4
2: StateReplicate match=3 next=4 score=200
3: StateReplicate match=3 next=4 score=255
heir=3 churn=1

# The leader is deposed right here (never ticked again): 2 still believes
# *itself* is heir (stale); 3 correctly believes *itself* is heir (fresh).
# Both therefore use the fast heir-biased timeout (electionTimeout + tiny
# jitter, deterministic at exactly electionTimeout with these defaults) and
# fire in the same round, before either has heard from the other.
tick-election 2
----
ok

tick-election 3
----
ok

# Both are already candidates (term 2) before any message crosses between
# them. Each has voted for itself in term 2, so each rejects the other's
# MsgVote -- a genuine split vote, exactly like vanilla Raft's own
# split-candidacy case.
stabilize 2 3
----

1: StateLeader (Voter) Term:1 Lead:1
2: StateCandidate (Voter) Term:2 Lead:0
3: StateCandidate (Voter) Term:2 Lead:0

# Round two: heir belief was cleared on both sides by the term bump above
# (T4.4's "heir cleared on term change"), so both are back to vanilla
# timeouts. Pin them apart deterministically -- 3 fires well within one
# tick-election round, 2 does not -- standing in for "resolved by
# randomized jitter" without depending on the real PRNG.
set-randomized-election-timeout 2 timeout=10
----
ok

set-randomized-election-timeout 3 timeout=2
----
ok

tick-election 3
----
ok

tick-election 2
----
ok

# 3 campaigns alone at the higher term; 2 (still a stale term-2 candidate)
# sees the higher term, steps down, and grants -- same log, hasn't voted at
# this term yet. Clean resolution, no thrashing.
stabilize 2 3
